headline: Anthropic's filing timeline firms up; EU code of practice settles into enforcement

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's ten to one UTC on Friday, October thirtieth. This is Aradio, with two updates since the last bulletin.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: A second report says Anthropic is preparing a confidential filing before the end of the year. Alphabet is not part of this story, but the timing matters for every lab raising money.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The company declined to comment. Until a filing is confirmed, this stays reported, not settled.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: In Brussels, the AI Office published its first supervisory priorities under the code of practice for general-purpose models.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: No new signatories this week, so we are marking that story steady.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Watch for the first formal information requests to model providers.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On Anthropic, the detail that matters is the confidential route. A confidential submission lets the company respond to regulators' comments before anything is public, so the first hard evidence may be weeks away.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Two independent reports on timing are more than we had on Monday, but it is still the press reading tea leaves, not the company speaking.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Our model ticket on the listing stays at reported. We will move it when there is a filing, a bank on the record, or a statement from the company.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Back to Brussels for a moment. The supervisory priorities name documentation of training data and evaluations of systemic risk as the first areas the office will check.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That lines up with what the code already asks for, which is why the labs that signed are calling it a non-event. The labs that did not sign are the ones to watch.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's Aradio. We'll be back when the picture changes.
